title: Forge Workers current revision
audience: CloudX implementers reviewing directory trust and embedded worker terminals

sections.title: Current revision: verified directory trust and worker terminals inside Forge

claims.text: Forge automatically prepares private managed checkouts and authenticates Git using connected identities without local checkout configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Creates a private checkout under dataDir/forge-workers/checkouts, initializes its Git repository, fetches the exact base/head using an authorization header and excludes credentials from origin URL.
Runtime settings require remote repository/templates rather than a local repositoryPath; Git access resolves the connected role credentials.

claims.text: Explicit repository approval grants trust only to canonical Forge-owned checkouts for the matching provider, API URL and configured repository; authorization checks current and captured checkout ownership on each materialization.

evidence.excerpt: Saved approval must equal the supplied repository and the currently configured repository.
Server-only callback checks approval, current ownership record and captured checkout/.git identities and Git configuration hash.
Authorization callback is evaluated before overlay creation, including context refresh.

claims.text: The exact checkout trust entry is written only in the worker Codex overlay; source configuration and unrelated project decisions are preserved, and an explicit untrusted decision for the checkout rejects the grant.

evidence.excerpt: Parses source config into an isolated overlay, checks canonical cwd, rejects untrusted exact key, and adds trust_level=trusted only at that key.

evidence.locator: exact worker cwd trust and source policy tests
evidence.excerpt: Tests preserve source text, reject explicit untrusted policy and prevent public metadata from authorizing trust.

claims.text: Workers appear as selectable subtabs inside Forge; View worker selects the worker there, selection uses the stable worker identity across resumed terminal replacement, and server-owned sessions are excluded from top-level workspace placement.

evidence.excerpt: Selects by worker ID, validates Forge owner plus matching session/worker metadata, renders the terminal only in the focused Forge pane.
View worker sets the selected worker ID and opens the Workers section.
createTab receives server-only ownerPluginId=forge independently of repository trust.
Owned embedded sessions publish without pane placement.
Owner comes from server launch options; embedded sessions remain in session snapshots but cannot become active top-level tabs.
Worker recovery and lifecycle control require server-assigned ownerPluginId=forge as well as matching worker metadata and cwd.

claims.text: Installed Codex 0.153.4 passed seven native PTY trust scenarios without model requests. Exact overlay trust loads project configuration. Parent trust and quoted dotted CLI keys do not grant checkout trust.

evidence.excerpt: Seven passing scenarios, clean process exits, zero local model requests; initialized composer confirmed by model marker and unsent input.
Selects exact cwd before Git root; no arbitrary ancestor project lookup.
Splits key path on every dot; does not interpret quoted TOML key segments.

claims.text: A confirmed failure before Codex process startup clears the pending-launch record so the existing checkout can be recovered. Ambiguous launch outcomes remain blocked.

evidence.excerpt: Clears launchPending only for the typed confirmed pre-process failure.
Only pre-spawn materialization failure is wrapped as PluginSessionNotStartedError.

evidence.locator: can recover and launch after a verified pre-process trust rejection
evidence.excerpt: After the typed error, recover returns the existing workspace and a subsequent launch succeeds.

claims.text: Nested worker UI checks passed 77 tests in four files. Desktop and mobile browser fixtures verified input, switching, paused output and resumed-session replacement with actual xterm and no page errors or overflow.

evidence.excerpt: Exact commands and original log/script/screenshot hashes; production UI with deterministic socket/hook transport at 1320x1000 and 390x844.

claims.text: The revision passed 2359 tests in 120 files with four test workers. Typecheck, all workspace builds and 12 shipped-shell browser tests passed.

evidence.excerpt: Exact commands, original log hashes and selected output. Two earlier timing failures and a passing 195-test focused rerun are recorded separately.

claims.text: After ownership recovery succeeds, unfinished issues resume their preserved checkouts with fresh context. Merged issues and review workers finish cleanup without relaunching. Failed resource checks still block resumption.

evidence.excerpt: Performs recoverResources before branching to cleanup for merged issue/review; unfinished issue continues normal launch without preparing a replacement checkout.
Unpublished and published issue recovery failures remain blocked; repaired ownership resumes retained checkout with latest feedback. Review/merged issue cleanup never relaunches.
Focused workflow and plugin tests: 31 passed.
Issue cleanup_failed uses Resume; review cleanup_failed uses Clean up.

claims.text: Worker context ownership uses a private directory identity, so atomic log rotation does not invalidate recovery. Cleanup rechecks that identity and preserves replacement directories.

evidence.excerpt: Context service mints a private per-tab directory and atomically rotates context.md inside it; returns a copy of its recorded directory identity.
Embedded sessions request owned context directories; Forge obtains the minted identity through the server session service.
Persists the minted directory identity, verifies before close, and reopens/removes only with the expected device/inode.
Opens parent and child directories with no-follow flags; checks expected identity and uses directory descriptors for child operations.

evidence.locator: cleans a paused worker after log rotation and a server restart
evidence.excerpt: Real PTY output rotates context-file inode; pause and SessionStore disposal precede runtime recovery/cleanup; owned checkout remains.

claims.text: Embedded worker context storage uses owned directories. Earlier flat context-file records are not converted or adopted as directory ownership.

evidence.excerpt: Creates a new private per-tab directory exclusively and retains only the identity minted during creation.
Requires the session-minted context directory identity, then reopens the recorded path as a directory with expected device/inode.

claims.text: A live GitHub issue worker resumed its retained checkout after resource recovery. Native Codex worked without a trust prompt; source configuration stayed unchanged and desktop/mobile terminals remained inside Forge.

evidence.excerpt: Exact browser command and artifact hashes, selected finalRefresh/finalBrowser booleans, visually inspected desktop/mobile screenshots of actual gpt-6-astra activity.

blocks.text: Forge prepares managed remote checkouts and shows each issue or review worker as a tab inside Forge. **View worker** selects its controls and terminal. Worker selection survives Resume replacing the terminal session; server-owned worker sessions stay outside workspace pane layouts.

Explicit repository approval matches the provider, API URL and current repository settings. Before granting trust, Forge checks both the current ownership record and the captured checkout identity. Changed ownership, Git configuration or approval prevents the grant.

The worker’s private Codex overlay receives the exact canonical checkout trust entry. Source configuration and other project trust decisions remain unchanged; an explicit untrusted checkout decision is preserved. Confirmed failures before process startup leave the checkout recoverable. Uncertain launches retain their ownership records.

Worker context logs now rotate inside a private directory whose identity comes from the session service. Forge records that directory identity and verifies it during recovery and cleanup. The real PTY regression rotates the log, stops the worker, recreates the runtime and removes the old terminal artifacts while retaining the checkout.
Embedded worker context storage changes from a flat file to an owned directory. Earlier context-file records are not adopted or converted automatically.

Once ownership and process checks succeed, an unfinished issue can resume in its preserved checkout with fresh context. Merged issues and review workers only finish cleanup; they do not launch another terminal. Failed checks continue to preserve resources.

Installed Codex 0.153.4 passed seven native PTY startup scenarios. Exact overlay trust loaded project configuration and reached the initialized composer; parent-only trust still showed the trust dialog. The checks made no model requests.

Nested worker UI checks passed 77 tests in four files. Desktop and mobile browser fixtures verified terminal input, worker switching, paused output retention and resumed-session replacement. They used the production terminal component and reported no page errors or horizontal overflow.

The current revision passed `npm test -- --reporter=dot --maxWorkers=4`: 2,359 tests in 120 files. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and all 12 shipped-shell browser tests also passed. The audit retains earlier timing failures and a snapshot failure caused by concurrent documentation editing, together with their passing reruns.

A live GitHub issue worker resumed in its retained checkout after resource recovery. Codex worked without the trust prompt, and the source configuration and production service stayed unchanged. Desktop and mobile checks showed its terminal inside Forge, with no page errors or horizontal overflow.
